candidates.title: Referee model accepts bisection openings, seals, leaf proofs and timeout wins only from a claim's posters, while Dave accepts every one of these moves from any address (variant of R1-A2-2 at the match-move sites)
candidates.component: PRT referee model in doc/recipes (prt.lua reveal_divergence, seal_divergence, settle_uarch_state_hash, emit_win_match_by_timeout; game-transport.lua accept_scheduled_response audience check) vs Dave v3.0.0-alpha.7 Tournament.sol (advanceMatch, sealLeafMatch, sealInnerMatchAndCreateInnerTournament, winLeafMatch, winMatchByTimeout)
candidates.role: Referee model (both components). Dave is the deployed referee; prt.lua stands in for the manual's normative model.
candidates.location: doc/recipes/prt.lua:602-627 (reveal request to subscription_hash(tournament.id, turn_claim)), :633-653 (seal request to the on-turn claim's posters), :368-382 (timeout-win request only to subscription_hash(tournament.id, other_claim)), :409-451 (state-transition proof request only to the posters of the two claims); doc/recipes/game-transport.lua:925-939 (accept_scheduled_response drops any reply whose connection is not in future.audience); bugs/harness/work/dave/released/prt/contracts/src/tournament/Tournament.sol:246-284, 298-367, 528-665, 677-732 (no msg.sender check on any match move; only the data is checked against the commitments).
candidates.description: In the referee model, a request about a claim goes only to the connections that posted that claim, and replies from anyone else are dropped before validation. Openings and seals go to the on-turn claim's posters. A timeout win goes to the waiting claim's posters. A leaf proof goes to the posters of the two claims. In Dave each of these moves is permissionless, so any address that knows the data can make it, and only the data is checked. The two therefore derive different results when the posters of a claim are silent but someone else holds valid data. (a) Timeout window: in the model the match ends in elimination at eliminable_at. In Dave any address can call winMatchByTimeout with the survivor's children, which are public from its join, so the survivor wins. (b) Sealed uarch leaf: in the model both claims are eliminated. In Dave any address can prove the unique transition with winLeafMatch, so the claim that committed to the true after-state survives. The manual follows the model ('any holder of that claim may answer it', 'a holder of the waiting claim may claim a timeout win') and does not list this difference among the PRT simplifications at the end of 'Running the tournament'. R1-A2-2 reported the same divergence for uarch-tournament joins only.
candidates.trigger: Any claimant abandons a claim that it alone posted, and a third party holds the claim's data (for timeout wins this is just the commitment's two children, which are emitted at join).
candidates.reachability: Reachable in any dispute: abandonment and Sybil posting are adversary capabilities (THREAT_MODEL section 7: 'Post any number of claims (Sybils) ... and abandon or defend them at will').
candidates.rating_steps: 1. Out of scope? No exclusion applies. The referee model and Dave are both in scope, and section 3 says that for the referee model 'Which claim a timeout or an elimination decides is part of what it derives.' 2. Role: Referee model, both for the deployed Dave contracts and for prt.lua (AUDIT.md component table). Section 5: 'Any other disagreement between a deployed referee and the model is a defect in one of the two.' The manual sides with the model, so section 3 rates the defect 'as if the manual were right', which makes it a defect of Dave in who may move. 3. High/Medium cases: none of the listed cases fits. 4. Critical: there is no threat to the goal. Every move is still checked against the claim's own commitment, so Dave's extra permissiveness only lets more parties defend a claim with correct data. The honest operator posts the honest claim itself, so it is always a holder in the model and can always move in Dave. Neither component can eliminate the honest claim or decide it by someone else's data. The literal reading of section 5 ('Any other disagreement ... is a defect') would make any violation at a reachable state Critical under step 4, which overstates a difference with no effect on the goal. 5. Low: a real disagreement between the deployed referee and the normative model, with no effect on settlement. If triage reads the section 5 disagreement clause as a rule under step 4, the class would be higher. That rests only on that reading, not on any effect on the goal.
candidates.claimed_severity: Low (the section 5 disagreement clause read as a rule would rate it higher; the deciding fact is that no input sequence lets either rule eliminate a claim that an honest holder defends)
candidates.threat_to_goal: None found. Both referees still settle on the honest claim whenever the honest operator defends it. The finding is a mismatch between the normative model and the deployed referee on which claim a timeout or an undefended leaf decides when the claim's posters are silent.
candidates.evidence: Code reading only. The manual's list of simplifications (doc/README.md around line 11308) names the rounds, the immediate uarch propagation, bonds and the leaf-race deadline, but not who may make match moves.
candidates.test_idea: Run the referee model (game-test-server style) with two quitter claims and a third player that holds claim B's children but did not post B. When A's opening times out, the third player sends a timeout win for B. The model must accept it, as Dave's winMatchByTimeout does. The test fails today because the reply is outside future.audience and is ignored. A Foundry counterpart shows winMatchByTimeout succeeding from a non-joining address.

notes: Traced in Dave v3.0.0-alpha.7 (released): joinTournament (requireFinalState at the last leaf, contested final state, ClockAlreadyInitialized blocking the same root twice, so a front-run honest root is still defensible by anyone), advanceBisection/sealDivergence (left-first descent, revealer parity, agree proof at d-1 against the revealing commitment, initialHash at d=0), toCycle and the counter-to-form map of CartesiStateTransition at 54/38 with log2step 38/0, MatchClocks classification (bisection, leaf race, sealed inner NONE), pauseWinnerAt/pauseAfterResponseAt positivity, childReturnAllowance, innerResult/winnerExpired/ELIMINABLE, winInnerTournament/eliminateInnerTournament (recorded child only, finished child immutable), pairCommitment and deleteMatch, factory clones via CREATE (no address front-running), DaveConsensus staging/sentries/provideMerkleRootOfInput. I found no way for a dishonest claim or move to eliminate, mispair or decide the honest claim.

Confirmed by reasoning, for the open question noted under A3 in round 1: provideMerkleRootOfInput reading the current epoch's bounds cannot reach an older epoch's leaf proof. A root match sealed into a child is deleted only once the child is finished (innerResult WINNER or ELIMINABLE both need _timeFinished). A finished tournament never resumes (joins need !closed, every other mutator needs !finished). The root must finish before staging and acceptance. So no leaf match of epoch N can run after epoch N+1 is sealed. Orphan clones (factory.instantiateInner is permissionless) can call the provider but nothing consumes their results.

Traced in prt.lua: validate_claim_response, partition_claims (merging, join order, clocks), new_match/advance_bisection/validate_bisection_response/validate_seal_response (match Dave), open_uarch_tournament (contested final states, initial = agreed state, allowance = max), settle_divergence/propagate_uarch_result, settle_timeout windows (equal to Dave's survivor rule), validate_state_transition_response forms. cartesi.keccak256 with two arguments rejects inputs that are not 32 bytes, and verify_slice requires integer sizes, so the decoding of hashes and integers in responses cannot change a decision.

vg.lua referee bisection (request_bisections, isolate_state_transition, request_state_transitions): last_agreed_hash is always a unanimous hash that includes the honest player's, so the before-hash is canonical. Each round eliminates at least one wrong player.
not_covered: No on-chain or EVM experiment was run. All conclusions come from reading code.

The Dave delay bound under Sybil populations: how many sequential matches async pairing can force on the honest claim, given that each child lasts at least its allowance (prt-delay-bound.md not read). This bears on A7 and on the threat model's 'logarithmic number of matches'.
Bond and refund economics (honest funding of a join bond in every inner tournament, draining of refund reserves), which the threat model does not address.

The honest PRT player's answers at every position a dishonest move can steer to (bundle boundaries, fixed-point padding, empty input slots after the last input or after an epoch-stopping input, uarch claims for periods past a fixed point), and the forest and bundle opening code. Read in part, not exercised.

prt-bridge.lua event-to-move translation (checked responder parity, leftNode/leftOfTwo, segmentStartPosition, the winLeafMatch cycle and the expected final state, and join front-running handling). Gas, nonce and fee paths were not checked.

Clock-only differences between prt.lua and Dave (no winner charge as in pauseWinnerAt, no childReturnAllowance) were noted but not reported. By section 3 they would be support/Low.
